chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not let the one whose arms are wide with blood impress you, for indeed Allah has for him a killer who does not die.'

key_terms.رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعَيْنِ بِالدَّمِ: One whose two arms are wide/enthusiastic with blood — an idiomatic expression for someone eager or practiced in killing
key_terms.قَاتِلًا لَا يَمُوتُ: A killer who does not die — divine retribution or the undying consequence of unjust killing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about those who are eager to shed blood?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) transmits a saying of the Prophet (SAWW) cautioning against admiring those who are enthusiastic killers or those who shed blood freely. The Arabic expression 'rahb al-dhira'ayn bi al-dam' (one with arms wide in blood) describes someone who embraces killing readily or whose hands are saturated with blood. The Prophet warns that God has appointed an undying 'killer' — understood as divine retribution or the inevitable consequences in the afterlife — that will deal with such a person. This narration belongs to the 'Chapter on Killing' (Kitab al-Diyat) in al-Kafi, addressing jurisprudential and ethical dimensions of unlawful killing.
